questions.question: Which description fits the **Appointment** resource?
options: A booking of a healthcare event among patient(s), practitioner(s), related person(s) and/or device(s) for a specific date/time.
A slot of time on a schedule that may be available for booking appointments.
A container for slots of time that may be available for booking appointments.
A reply to an appointment request for a patient and/or practitioner(s), such as a confirmation or rejection.
questions.explanation: **Appointment**: A booking of a healthcare event among patient(s), practitioner(s), related person(s) and/or device(s) for a specific date/time. This may result in one or more Encounter(s). The other descriptions belong to **Slot**, **Schedule**, **AppointmentResponse**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? Book the patient in with Dr Lee on Thursday at 10:00.
questions.explanation: **Appointment**. A planned meeting. When it happens, the actual visit is an Encounter.

questions.question: You know **Appointment**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “free time that can be booked”?
questions.explanation: **Slot**: free time that can be booked. **Appointment** is for something else: A booking of a healthcare event among patient(s), practitioner(s), related person(s) and/or device(s) for a specific date/time.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **Appointment** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of Appointment are `status` (1..1), `participant` (1..*). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **Appointment** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of Appointment: `status`. `status`: proposed | pending | booked | arrived | fulfilled | cancelled | noshow | entered-in-error | checked-in | waitlist. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
